+On 2026-08-13 the user confirmed that the failure occurs when one provider host launches another provider through CLI mode, such as Claude invoking Codex or Codex invoking Claude. A ten-minute caller timeout can detach or terminate observation even though the provider process may still be doing useful work. The related B-1be5 proposal only considered heuristic ledger provenance and does not solve this execution failure. During B-137a PLAN scope review, the first design was formally reopened because its evidence write ordering would either deadlock before terminal or let the controller impersonate the reviewer.
 
 ## Key Insights
+
 The framework must supervise the provider process at the actual execution boundary. A worker heartbeat and provider progress are different facts; output silence is diagnostic rather than terminal. Every wait must be bounded, every run must have a finite absolute deadline, and a durable next-touch reconciler must be able to materialize terminal truth even when the original worker becomes wedged. Formal reviewer evidence must bind to the exact managed receipt instead of provider plus story plus time-window guesses.
 
+Reviewer evidence also needs a two-phase provenance protocol. The provider reviewer authors an immutable proposal containing its pass/findings and truthful read evidence while the run is active. It cannot call the final evidence writer before the terminal receipt and evidence journal are sealed. After successful terminal, a mechanical importer validates the sealed proposal and imports it without allowing the controller to change the verdict or become the reviewer. The new composite evidence class must use the existing shared Proof Admissibility artifact registry, intake, reason vocabulary and evaluator at both write-time and REVIEW-gate consumption; a parallel special-case proof system is not acceptable.
+
 ## Solution Tradeoffs
-A single deep ManagedHostRun module adds durable runtime artifacts, worker continuation and reconciliation complexity, but removes duplicated foreground/background supervision and makes cancellation, cleanup and evidence semantics consistent. M1 execution safety and M2 gate evidence ship together so the framework does not claim enforcement while raw CLI reviews can still satisfy formal gates. Legacy configured provider timeout ceilings remain separate and unchanged.

The two-phase proposal/import protocol adds one post-terminal mechanical step, but preserves the actual provider reviewer as evidence author and prevents controller self-absolution. Reusing shared Proof Admissibility adds registry work but avoids a second trust vocabulary and keeps gate-consumed facts centrally auditable. +# B-137a implementation plan
+
+## Public seams and invariant order
+
+The behavior-facing seams are:
+1. `host_run` submit/foreground attach;
+2. `host_run_status(runId, waitMs<=30000)`;
+3. `host_run_cancel(runId, reason?)`;
+4. `cross_host_review` as the privileged verdict-profile owner;
+5. `review_pass_set` / `finding_add` plus the REVIEW gate as managed-evidence consumers.
+
+Private worker, file layout, launch adapters and reconciliation helpers are tested only through those seams or through real child-process effects. Each vertical slice follows RED → minimal GREEN; implementation does not bulk-create imagined internal tests.
+
+## CHK-001 — Persist and reconcile managed host-run lifecycle
+
+Create a deep `core/managed-host-run.ts` module whose small interface owns submit, attach/status projection, cancel, worker execution and reconcile. A run gets a generated `hrun_*` identity and an immutable root under `.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`.
+
+Submit writes immutable/spec-bound state atomically: `spec.json`, digest-only `owner.json`, 0600 one-shot `input.cap` and `input.prompt`, initial `snapshot.json`, and append-only `events.jsonl`. The hidden worker wins `claim.json` using exclusive create, validates the one-shot capability, unlinks both input files, marks `claimReady`, acquires provider admission, launches the private provider adapter and periodically advances `workerHeartbeatAt`. Provider output updates a separate `lastProviderProgressAt` only when observable; unsupported observability is represented as `unobservable`, never fabricated.
+
+A terminal is created exclusively and exactly once. It records outcome, timing, exit/timeout/cancel reason, provider identity, spec/profile binding digests, evidence journal digest, process cleanup facts, residual process state and an independent `replacementSafe`. Repeated status/cancel/attach calls first acquire a short `reconcile.lock`, re-read facts, and materialize terminal truth for deadline expiry or authoritative worker/provider death. Silence is never a transition predicate. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity yields honest residual `unknown` and `replacementSafe:false`, not blind termination.
+
+Initial RED tests cover: exclusive claim winner, unchanged running state across silent intervals, worker crash followed by deadline reconciliation, one terminal under concurrent reconcilers, idempotent status/cancel, terminal/result digest stability, capability/prompt deletion, and no automatic retry.
+
+## CHK-002 — Expose submit, attach, status and cancel command surfaces
+
+Extend the host-run command schema:
+- `host_run --detach` submits, waits only for a bounded claim handshake, and returns `runId/state/deadlineAt/generation`;
+- foreground `host_run` calls the same submit path then attaches to that run, projecting live output and final usage without owning the provider child;
+- `host_run_status --runId ... --waitMs ...` performs bounded long-poll, returning immediately on terminal or snapshot-generation change and otherwise after at most 30000ms;
+- `host_run_cancel --runId ... --reason ...` writes an idempotent cooperative request and reconciles;
+- hidden `host_run_worker --runId ...` is runtime-only and never advertised as an operator workflow.
+
+Declare command policy, process-fact level and CLI watchdog behavior for runtime continuation. A foreground caller/watchdog exit may end attachment but cannot convert the managed run to failed or cancel the worker. JSON stdout remains one machine object; text mode keeps live stream routing and concise status guidance. The handler never stores raw prompt/capability in argv or durable public artifacts.
+
+RED starts at CLI/handler seams: detach returns after claim, status wait is capped, foreground and detached share one run/receipt shape, cancel is idempotent, unknown run is fail-closed, and caller termination leaves the run queryable.
+
+## CHK-003 — Supervise provider processes portably and honestly
+
+Provider adapters remain private to ManagedHostRun and preserve canonical launcher specifications. Codex uses documented `codex exec ... -`, the worker writes the prompt to stdin and closes it. Claude and agy retain their canonical launcher contracts.
+
+On POSIX, spawn the provider as a new process group and persist PID/PGID plus a launch fingerprint. Cancellation/deadline cleanup is TERM → bounded grace → KILL → reap → residual probe. Identity is revalidated before signals. On unsupported platforms, managed execution refuses before provider spawn with a structured unsupported-platform terminal; it does not silently degrade to child-only cleanup.
+
+Move the first-output clock to diagnostics only. Preserve finite total timeout/deadline, bounded output projection, provider usage candidate extraction, turn-failure diagnostic, passthrough-degradation honesty and failure classification. Worker heartbeat and provider progress are distinct fields.
+
+RED uses real local Node subprocesses for silent completion, descendant cleanup and TERM-resistant escalation, plus injected provider adapters for Codex argv/stdin closure, overflow and parsing.
+
+## CHK-004 — Enforce shared provider admission independent of usage-ledger mode
+
+Extract the slot registry from the ledger-gated branch into one provider-admission module. Acquisition happens before every provider spawn regardless of `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER`; usage preflight/budget/final rows remain conditional and keep existing fail-closed/append-honesty semantics. Slot ownership token, dead-PID reclaim, corrupt-meta stale backstop and token-guarded release remain unchanged.
+
+Inventory production provider launch sites. Managed host_run and cross_host_review use ManagedHostRun admission. Direct Codex/Claude/Gemini leaves that cannot yet emit a managed receipt are explicitly `legacy_unmanaged` for lifecycle but still `admission_managed`; no launch site may be `admission_unmanaged`. Add a source registry/contract smoke so new direct spawn paths fail review until classified.
+
+Preserve candidate-spec per-chunk streaming, 64KiB discard-all overflow and null first-output diagnostics. RED covers ledger-off cap contention, dead/corrupt/live slot reclaim, release race, and source inventory completeness.
+
+## CHK-005 — Route cross-host review through managed execution
+
+Keep `cross_host_review` as profile owner. It still resolves the authoritative story worktree, captures clean HEAD/material/storyFiles facts, authorizes read-only Codex dispatch, creates the detached review snapshot, redacts environment, computes the existing policy timeout ceiling, constructs the structured-verdict prompt and validates the returned verdict schema.
+
+Replace only its direct provider execution with internal ManagedHostRun submit+attach using profile `cross-host-verdict` and opaque bindings. The terminal receipt is included in paired host-verdict provenance. Provider nonzero/timeout/cancel/admission refusal/invalid verdict continue to yield the existing honest blocked/error decision; no raw provider stdout becomes gate evidence.
+
+Protect configured `provider.codex`, `cross_host_review`, bounded retry and fail-closed policies with exact source/runtime regression assertions. RED captures the current direct leaf, then proves the managed path while all existing cross-host checks remain green.
+
+## CHK-006 — Bind formal reviewer evidence to exact managed receipts
+
+Add a versioned managed-execution binding and a two-phase provider-authored evidence protocol. The profile owner seals opaque bindings at submit: storyId, reviewRunId, lane, intended provider/transport, prompt-envelope/body/context/assembled digests, materialHash, headHash and storyFilesHash. While running, the provider reviewer writes exactly one immutable proposal into the evidence journal: pass or findings plus truthful readManifest/readLog and its registered reviewer identity. It does not call final `review_pass_set` or `finding_add`.
+
+Successful terminal creation seals the spec digest, proposal digest and append-only journal digest. After terminal, `managed_review_evidence_import` accepts only a runId/receipt reference, reads the sealed provider-authored bytes, and imports the existing ReviewPass/Finding shape while preserving agent/lane/reviewRun/read provenance exactly. It exposes no verdict/note/finding override fields, is idempotent, and refuses non-success terminal, residual/replacement ambiguity, missing/multiple proposals or any digest mismatch. The controller may trigger import but cannot become the reviewer or reinterpret its verdict.
+
+Register this managed receipt/composite evidence as a canonical artifact kind in shared Proof Admissibility with producer boundary, scope, REVIEW consumer, claim kind, temporal/material role, semantic field binding and canonical reason codes. Both import-time admission and the REVIEW gate must call the same shared registry/intake/evaluator; process-fact registry declares the gate semantics but is not a substitute. The gate revalidates current terminal, proposal/journal integrity, exact ReviewRun/lane/provider/prompt envelope and current material tuple instead of trusting persisted booleans.
+
+Native-host reviewer lanes retain their existing signed ReviewRun/pass/finding path and are not falsely described as mechanically supervised by ManagedHostRun. Main/implementer/controller-authored evidence, raw CLI output, usage-ledger rows, B-1be5-style time-window matching, pre-terminal proposals and structured degraded decisions cannot upgrade to normal managed receipt assurance.
+
+RED tests the valid provider proposal → successful terminal seal → importer → REVIEW gate path, plus forged runId/terminal/journal/proposal, stale/cross-story/cross-lane/cross-provider/material mismatch, raw CLI absence, controller override/self-assertion, multiple proposals, importer replay, and non-success terminal. A mutation/source-contract test proves both write-time and gate call the shared evaluator: bypassing either call or adding a parallel special-case evaluator must fail.
+
+## CHK-007 — Add adversarial coverage, observability, migration docs and rollout controls
+
+Create an auto-discovered aggregate smoke so no package.json script is needed. It runs focused managed lifecycle, command, real process-group, admission, cross-host and receipt-gate tests. Add bounded mutation bites that prove premature silence failure, terminal-only monitoring and forged receipt changes are caught. Avoid destructive shared-dist mutations during parallel review.

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017Wc19SHwGDCTsCzps8TrWz","type":"tool_result","content":"1	# Durable managed host runs, reviewer receipts, and usage diagnostics
2	
3	Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
4	`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
5	`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
6	until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
7	return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.
8	
9	The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
10	the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
11	admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
12	that never used the managed boundary.
13	
14	## Why this exists
15	
16	A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
17	probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
18	desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
19	`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
20	terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
21	`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
22	active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
23	one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
24	native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
25	their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.
26	
27	Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
28	workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
29	phase.
30	
31	## `host_run`
32	
33	```
34	lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
35	  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
36	  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
37	  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
38	  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
39	  [--json]
40	```
41	
42	`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
43	`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
44	run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:
45	
46	```bash
47	lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
48	lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
49	```
50	
51	`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
52	inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
53	only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
54	receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
55	never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
56	absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
57	touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
58	cleanup made replacement safe.
59	
60	The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
61	target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
62	the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
63	never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.
64	
65	Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
66	caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
67	projection is therefore bounded: once the ceiling is reached it reports
68	`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail. Worker heartbeat and
69	`lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
70	the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
71	only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
72	is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
73	is written to stderr, for example:
74	
75	```
76	usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
77	```
78	
79	Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
80	usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
81	capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
82	flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
83	poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
84	happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
85	retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
86	usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
87	rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
88	valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
89	later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
90	(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
91	perfectly good final usage event).

93	### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)
94	
95	| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
96	|---|---|---|---|
97	| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
98	| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |
99	
100	In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
101	delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
102	result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the projection is explicitly
103	truncated; the JSON `stdout` field carries only the bounded usage-parse tail,
104	not an unbounded or complete transcript.
105	
106	If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
107	but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
108	`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
109	`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
110	downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
111	delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
112	event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
113	stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
114	stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
115	contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
116	once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
117	skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
118	passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
119	outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
120	serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
121	by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
122	command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
123	from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
124	fires while a listener is attached.
125	
126	Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
127	runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
128	forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
129	non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
130	`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.

132	### Reviewer launch
133	
134	Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
135	when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
136	registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
137	lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
138	identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
139	registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
140	in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
141	attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
142	process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.
143	
144	An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
145	`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
146	review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
147	the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
148	direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
149	below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
150	capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
151	registered broker set.
152	
153	The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
154	ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
155	ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
156	view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
157	Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
158	matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
159	instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.

189	Inside the provider process, the managed prompt forbids `review_run_start`,
190	`review_pass_set` and `finding_add`. Its final assistant result must be exactly

192	pass-or-findings plus truthful read evidence. After a successful provider exit,
193	the managed adapter selects only Codex's terminal `item.completed`
194	`agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs, arbitrary streamed
195	stdout and controller fields are ignored. The worker validates the sealed
196	story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
197	Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized envelopes fail the run closed. The
198	`pass` form requires a non-empty note and no findings (an empty findings array is
199	equivalent to absence). The `findings` form requires at least one fully valid

202	can never become a formal finding or evidence field. The older
203	descriptor-authorized `managed_review_proposal_set` command remains a

210	`processCleanup.reaped=true`, and

234	`host_run_worker` is an internal continuation command. It remains dispatchable

259	## Binding conventions
260	
261	Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:
262	
263	| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
264	|---|---|---|
265	| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
266	| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
267	| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
268	| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
269	| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |
270	
271	`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
272	ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
273	before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
274	`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).
275	
276	When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
277	configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
278	`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
279	without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
280	custom `storyDir`.
281	
282	## Per-host usage semantics
283	
284	Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
285	`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.
286	
287	- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
288	  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
289	  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
290	  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
291	  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
292	  digested raw.
293	- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
294	  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
295	
296	A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
297	`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.
298	
299	同样的诚实口径适用于 reviewer A/B：缺少 exact per-role historical envelope、
300	reviewer output、adjudication bytes 或 provider receipt 时结果是
301	`INCONCLUSIVE`，不是“0 token”或已证明的节省。B-235e 的独立 replay campaign
302	因此不声称达到计划中的 50% incremental / 40% assembled 降幅。
303	
304	The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
305	that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
306	ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
307	skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
308	stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
309	`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to both managed hosts;
310	the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
311	provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
312	append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
313	`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
314	nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.
315	
316	The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
317	`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
318	`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
319	swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
320	non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
321	and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
322	`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
323	`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
324	minted for a blocked row that never persisted.

326	## Provider execution surfaces
327	
328	Every production provider spawn site carries a `ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus`
329	and is enumerated by `provider-execution-inventory-contract`, which fails if a
330	new spawn path appears unclassified:
331	
332	- `managed` — runs through ManagedHostRun (durable run identity, supervised
333	  process group, absolute deadline, one terminal receipt).
334	- `admission_only` — not managed-executed, but still routed through the shared
335	  admission boundary, so the concurrency cap below applies.
336	- `adapter_only` — a low-level adapter whose caller owns admission.
337	- `readiness_probe` — version/readiness checks only; never review evidence.
338	- `legacy_unmanaged` — neither managed nor admission-routed. Reserved and
339	  **currently empty by contract**: the inventory test asserts no surface uses
340	  it, so introducing one is a deliberate, reviewable act.
341	
342	There is no `admission_managed` status — admission and managed execution are
343	independent properties, spelled `admission_only` and `managed`.
344	
345	See `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` for
346	the decision record.
347	
348	## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)
349	
350	With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
351	is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
352	`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
353	reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
354	and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
355	still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
356	blocked row was persisted.
357	
358	- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
359	  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
360	  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
361	- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
362	  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
363	  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
364	  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
365	  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
366	  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
367	  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
368	  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
369	  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
370	  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
371	  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
372	  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
373	  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
374	  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
375	  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
376	  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
377	  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
378	  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
379	  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
380	  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
381	  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
382	  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
383	  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
384	  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
385	  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
386	  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
387	  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
388	  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
389	  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
390	  count drops below the new cap.
391	
392	Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
393	host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
394	a hard-coded default.
395	
396	The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
397	--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
398	modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the

Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.

The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
that never used the managed boundary.

## Why this exists

A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.

Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
phase.

## `host_run`

```
lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
  [--json]
```

`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:

```bash
lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
```

`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
cleanup made replacement safe.

The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.

Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
caller as it arrives, up to the per-run 8 MiB retention ceiling. The foreground
projection is therefore bounded: once the ceiling is reached it reports
`truncated=true` and does not promise the omitted tail. Worker heartbeat and
`lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
is written to stderr, for example:

```
usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
```

Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
perfectly good final usage event).

### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)

| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |

In `--json` mode the bounded host transcript (at most 8 MiB per managed run) is
delivered live on **stderr** so that **stdout stays clean** for the one JSON
result. If the transcript exceeds that ceiling, the projection is explicitly
truncated; the JSON `stdout` field carries only the bounded usage-parse tail,
not an unbounded or complete transcript.

If the live passthrough sink fails mid-run, delivery stops at the first failure
but the run, usage recording, and slot release still complete: text mode prints a
`host_run warning:` line to stderr and the `--json` result carries a non-null
`passthroughError` field. This holds for **both** failure shapes a closed
downstream pipe can take: a **synchronous** write throw, and — because Node
delivers pipe write failures like a real `EPIPE` as an **asynchronous `'error'`
event** on `process.stdout` / `process.stderr` rather than a throw — that async
stream error too. `host_run` attaches (and, in a `finally`, removes) its own
stdout/stderr `'error'` listeners for the duration of the run, so a real EPIPE is
contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are
skipped rather than risk a late unhandled `'error'`, and **every** live
passthrough chunk write *and* final diagnostic write is settle-aware:
outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
fires while a listener is attached.

Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.

### Reviewer launch

Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.

An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
registered broker set.

The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.

## Binding conventions

Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:

| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |

`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).

When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
custom `storyDir`.

## Per-host usage semantics

Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.

- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
  digested raw.
- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).

A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.

The one-line usage summary reflects the **actual append outcome**, not merely
that the provider envelope parsed. When the ledger append itself fails (a corrupt
ledger, or a lock-wait timeout that skips the write), the summary reports a
skipped state (`recorded: none`, reason `ledger_append_failed(...)`) and the
stderr line reads `usage: ledger_append_failed(...)` — it never claims
`usage recorded` for a row that never landed. This applies to both managed hosts;
the provider is still surfaced for attribution, but token counts stay null. A
provider record that BUILT fine but whose append failed is reported as an
append failure keyed on the parsed usage — it is **never degraded to
`source=unavailable`** (which would falsely read as "the provider reported
nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.

The same honesty gate covers the **blocked rows**: a cap refusal claims
`recorded: blocked` (and, for a concurrency refusal, surfaces the blocked row's
`recordId`) only when the blocked row **actually appended**. When that append is
swallowed too, the refusal itself is unchanged — still fail-closed, no spawn,
non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`
and a composed reason that keeps the refusal visible, e.g.
`hard_budget_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)` or
`concurrency_cap_exceeded (...); ledger_append_failed(...)`. A recordId is never
minted for a blocked row that never persisted.

## Provider execution surfaces

Every production provider spawn site carries a `ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus`
and is enumerated by `provider-execution-inventory-contract`, which fails if a
new spawn path appears unclassified:

- `managed` — runs through ManagedHostRun (durable run identity, supervised
  process group, absolute deadline, one terminal receipt).
- `admission_only` — not managed-executed, but still routed through the shared
  admission boundary, so the concurrency cap below applies.
- `adapter_only` — a low-level adapter whose caller owns admission.
- `readiness_probe` — version/readiness checks only; never review evidence.
- `legacy_unmanaged` — neither managed nor admission-routed. Reserved and
  **currently empty by contract**: the inventory test asserts no surface uses
  it, so introducing one is a deliberate, reviewable act.

There is no `admission_managed` status — admission and managed execution are
independent properties, spelled `admission_only` and `managed`.

See `docs/requirements/decisions/managed-cross-provider-cli-execution.md` for
the decision record.

## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)

With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
blocked row was persisted.

- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`
  holds **fixed numbered slots** `slot-0.json` .. `slot-(cap-1).json`, one per
  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.
  The lock makes the live-count check, stale reclaim, cap-lowering check and
  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index
  under `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_MAX_CONCURRENT` (default **4**; unset / invalid /
  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
  count drops below the new cap.

Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the managed
host that was asked to run (`openai` for codex or `anthropic` for claude), never
a hard-coded default.

The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
after the run.

The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.

Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
carries the releaser's own token.

There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.

Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.

## Diagnostics, cleanup, and trust boundary

`lattice doctor --full` lists every managed run with state, worker liveness,
worker heartbeat, provider progress mode/time, deadline, cancellation,
residual-process status, `replacementSafe`, and retention state. `lattice
doctor --repair` removes heavy terminal run directories only after the 90-day
retention window and first archives the sealed minimal receipt plus imported
evidence-binding digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Active or
corrupt runs and any directory still carrying one-shot inputs are retained
fail-closed for inspection; failed launch/claim paths erase prompt, capability,
and one-shot environment immediately. The imported binding carries a separate
immutable digest seal, so a shape-preserving binding rewrite is corrupt before
doctor/GC can delete it. Expired cross-host runs also remove only their canonical
`lattice-xhr-review-*/worktree` snapshot; paths outside that tmp boundary fail
closed. Per-run live output is capped at 8 MiB;
status readers page bounded frames and surface truncation rather than loading an
unbounded transcript.

The runtime directory is local and mode 0700; sensitive one-shot files are 0600.
This protects against other users under ordinary filesystem permissions, not a
same-UID/root attacker. Operators must treat retained live output as locally
sensitive. Native Codex/Claude subagent APIs are deliberately out of scope:
ManagedHostRun owns only cross-provider CLI processes launched by Proofbound.

## `usage_sweep` (read-only retro-attribution)

```
lattice usage_sweep --since 2026-07-01 [--json]
```

`usage_sweep` stream-reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` since a cutoff and reports per-session token
totals, originator (desktop vs exec vs claude-code), cwd, first/last timestamps,
and `B-xxxx` story mentions, plus a per-story rollup and grand totals. It exists
to make runs that never went through `host_run` (interactive desktop sessions in
particular) at least visible.

- The report header states **NON-AUTHORITATIVE ESTIMATE** prominently in both
  the human table and `--json`. The totals come from host transcript stores, not
  billing truth.
- It performs **no ledger backfill**: swept sessions are never written into the
  usage ledger.
- It is strictly **read-only**. The only write it can perform is an explicit
  `--out <path>` JSON report, and that write is create-only and fenced:
  - `--out` must be a **relative** path that resolves inside the project root;
    absolute paths and any `..` traversal escaping the root are refused
    outright.
  - It only ever **creates a new report file** — the file is opened with the
    exclusive-create `wx` flag, so an already-existing target is refused
    atomically and `usage_sweep` can never overwrite or truncate anything
    (not even via a symlink at the target path).
  - It refuses to write through **symlinked ancestor directories**, and the
    resolved real path must still fall inside the (realpath'd) project root,
    so an inside-root symlink cannot redirect the report outside the project.
  - Missing report directories are created only **after** all of those checks
    pass.
  - Because `--out` writes a file into the material tree, a **non-empty `--out`
    is dynamically classified `storyScopedMutating`** by the ownership gate
    (F-014), so it is refused in read-only reviewer mode
    (`LATTICE_REVIEWER_READONLY=1`) and on a retired root; without `--out`,
    `usage_sweep` stays read-only and runnable by any session.
  - The **same `--out` boundary governs the CLI activity / hook layer** (F-028):
    a plain (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` is read-only there too, so it runs **no
    pre/post command hooks** and writes **no activity-log entry by default** (the
    `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_RECORD_READONLY=1` read-only heartbeat override documented
    in docs/CLI.md still applies); a non-empty `--out` is treated as a write and
    runs the hooks + records activity like any other mutating command.
  - The same boundary also governs the **codex process-event surface** (F-032):
    under `LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex` cli-engine appends a `codex_cli` event
    to the active story's `process-events.jsonl` after a command. That append is
    STORY metadata, so it obeys the identical read-only contract — a plain
    (no-`--out`) `usage_sweep` appends **no process event** (even with an
    inferred active story), while a non-empty `--out` (a write) records the
    process event like any other mutating command. The owner-lease heartbeat is
    intentionally exempt: it is keyed on the ownership class (only a
    `storyScopedMutating`/`dangerousMutating` write touches the lease), never on
    this read-only classification, so read-only session upkeep is unaffected.

## Non-goals

- Usage rows **never gate the workflow** — they are `gateEvidence=false`
  diagnostics and are not consumed by any REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority gate.
- Interactive desktop host sessions are **out of reach** of the choke point;
  they are report-only via `usage_sweep`, never through `host_run`.
- `usage_sweep` never mutates story, ledger, or lifecycle state and never
  backfills the ledger.

22	
23	Proofbound owns every public `host_run` and every formal cross-provider CLI
24	reviewer launch through a durable `ManagedHostRun`. General provider workloads
25	such as planned steps and autopilot repair keep their existing bounded adapters
26	but share the mandatory provider-process admission registry; they do not claim
27	durable reviewer ownership or reviewer evidence. The caller submits and
28	observes; a detached worker owns the managed provider process until an exclusive
29	terminal record exists.
30	
31	The public surface is:
32	
33	- `host_run`: submit, optionally attach in foreground, or return after claim
34	  with `--detach`;
35	- `host_run_status`: read or long-poll one run for at most 30 seconds;
36	- `host_run_cancel`: idempotently request cancellation;
37	- `host_run_worker`: private runtime continuation, dispatchable internally but
38	  hidden from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
39	- `managed_review_proposal_set`: compatibility-only provider callback for older
40	  adapters, not the formal managed happy path;
41	- `managed_review_evidence_import`: verdict-free exact-receipt importer.

47	## State and liveness contract
48	
49	The states are `submitted`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and
50	`timed_out`. Exactly one terminal file wins by exclusive creation. Repeated
51	status, cancel and resume operations are idempotent and never create a new run.
52	
53	Two clocks are deliberately distinct:
54	
55	- `workerHeartbeatAt` shows that the supervisor can still update its durable
56	  snapshot;
57	- `lastProviderProgressAt` changes only when observable provider stdout/stderr
58	  arrives.
59	
60	Neither clock is a completion oracle. A provider may legitimately be silent,
61	and a worker heartbeat does not prove provider progress. Expiry of a 30-second
62	observation wait is non-terminal: it only wakes the caller and never authorizes
63	a retry. The `host_run_status` call is also the run's next-touch reconciler,
64	however, so during that call an already-requested cancellation or an expired
65	absolute deadline can legitimately publish the corresponding `cancelled` or
66	`timed_out` terminal state.
67	
68	Every run has a finite absolute deadline (30 minutes by default, bounded to 24
69	hours). Deadline or cancellation reconciliation performs bounded TERM, KILL,
70	reap and residual probing. Replacement is safe only when cleanup facts prove
71	there is no residual process group. Ambiguous PID/PGID identity remains
72	`replacementSafe=false`; it is not guessed away.

74	## Persistence and process ownership
75	
76	Each run has a 0700 directory at
77	`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
78	primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
79	DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
80	bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
81	capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
82	Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
83	the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
84	runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.
85	
86	On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
87	prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`). Claude receives a 0600
88	one-shot prompt file below the exact provider cwd's ignored
89	`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/` tree, because Claude's workspace sandbox
90	rejects an otherwise protected OS-temp prompt outside that cwd. Prompt text never

92	Claude reviewer has no approval terminal, so only the signed `managed_reviewer`
93	profile launches it with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ordinary Claude
94	host runs retain their configured policy, and the strict final proposal/parser

97	exposes a stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms
98	likewise refuse before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup
99	is equivalent.

101	## Shared provider admission
102	
103	Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
104	of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
105	token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
106	Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
107	not process admission.
108	
109	A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
110	reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
111	checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
112	already been reclaimed and reassigned.
113	
114	Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
115	admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
116	review evidence.

119	
120	Every production provider spawn site is classified by
121	`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),

## Persistence and process ownership

Each run has a 0700 directory at
`<primary-worktree>/.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`. Resolving to the
primary worktree keeps the run observable after a Story worktree is removed at
DONE. Immutable spec and digest-only owner data, snapshot, append-only events,
bounded live output, result and terminal receipt are durable. Live output is
capped at 8 MiB per run and reports truncation instead of growing without bound.
Prompt, capability and optional redacted environment are 0600 one-shot inputs;
the worker validates and deletes them before provider launch. Only root and
runId cross the detached-worker argv boundary.

On POSIX the provider runs in an isolated process group. Codex receives the
prompt through documented stdin (`codex exec ... -`). Claude receives a 0600
one-shot prompt file below the exact provider cwd's ignored
`.lattice/runtime/host-run-prompts/` tree, because Claude's workspace sandbox
rejects an otherwise protected OS-temp prompt outside that cwd. Prompt text never
enters argv and the private leaf is removed after settlement. A detached formal
Claude reviewer has no approval terminal, so only the signed `managed_reviewer`
profile launches it with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; ordinary Claude
host runs retain their configured policy, and the strict final proposal/parser
boundary is unchanged. The current agy print launcher accepts prompt text only
in argv, so managed agy execution refuses before provider spawn until agy
exposes a stdin or protected prompt-file transport. Unsupported platforms
likewise refuse before provider spawn rather than pretending child-only cleanup
is equivalent.

## Shared provider admission

Provider capacity is owned by `core/provider-process-registry.ts`, independent
of the usage ledger. All Proofbound-owned provider workloads acquire an atomic,
token-owned slot under `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/` before spawn.
Turning off `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER` disables usage rows and budget accounting,
not process admission.

A live recorded pid is never reclaimed because of age. Dead pids are
reclaimable; corrupt/ownerless slots use a bounded stale backstop. Release
checks the acquire token so a late old holder cannot delete a slot that has
already been reclaimed and reassigned.

Low-level provider adapter modules remain `adapter_only`: their caller owns
admission. Readiness/version probes are classified separately and do not become
review evidence.

### Provider execution surface classification

Every production provider spawn site is classified by
`ProviderExecutionSurfaceStatus` (`packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts`),
and `packages/main/src/tasks/provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts` fails if a
new spawn path appears without one:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `managed` | Executes through ManagedHostRun: durable run identity, supervised process group, absolute deadline, exactly one terminal receipt. |
| `admission_only` | Not managed-executed, but routed through the shared provider admission boundary, so the concurrency cap and slot accounting still apply. |
| `adapter_only` | A low-level adapter module whose *caller* owns admission; the adapter itself makes no gate claim. |
| `readiness_probe` | Version/readiness probing only. Never becomes review evidence. |
| `legacy_unmanaged` | A provider spawn that is neither managed nor admission-routed. **Reserved, and currently empty by contract.** |

`admission_managed` is not a status value: admission and managed execution are
two separate properties, expressed by `admission_only` (admission without
managed execution) and `managed` (both).

The `legacy_unmanaged` bucket exists so an unmanaged spawn path must be declared
rather than pass silently. It is asserted empty — `provider-execution-inventory-contract.ts`
requires that no surface carries it — so adding one is a deliberate, reviewable
act that fails the contract until justified. It is not a claim that unmanaged
execution is impossible, only that none is currently admitted.

## Formal managed reviewer evidence

Native-host reviewers retain the existing signed ReviewRun plus direct
ReviewPass/Finding flow. A cross-provider CLI reviewer uses a two-phase flow:

1. The controller creates the signed ReviewRun.
2. `host_run --managedReview` derives the exact assembled prompt and seals
   story, provider, lane, ReviewRun, head, material, story-files and prompt
   bindings.
3. The managed prompt requires the provider's final assistant result to be one
   bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope with
   pass-or-findings and truthful read evidence. It cannot write final
   `review_pass_set`/`finding_add` evidence from inside the managed run. After a
   successful provider exit, the owning adapter selects only Codex's terminal
   `item.completed` `agent_message` or Claude's successful terminal
   provider-validated `structured_output`; Claude's signed managed-review launch
   supplies a bounded non-secret `--json-schema` bound to the exact
   story/provider/lane/ReviewRun tuple. Tool logs, arbitrary stdout, Claude prose
   or fenced JSON, and controller fields are never proposal inputs. The worker
   validates the same tuple and atomically writes the immutable proposal.
   Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized final envelopes fail the managed
   run closed. The older descriptor-authorized
   `managed_review_proposal_set` callback remains compatibility-only.
4. Successful terminal creation seals spec, proposal, result, live-output and
   event-journal digests plus cleanup facts.
5. The controller calls `managed_review_evidence_import` with only the exact
   runId and receiptId. It cannot provide or alter verdict bytes. Import still
   fails closed unless the completed receipt proves `replacementSafe=true`,
   `processCleanup.reaped=true`, and
   `processCleanup.residualProcessGroup=false`.
6. The importer preserves provider reviewer/lane/ReviewRun/read provenance and
   writes the existing signed ReviewPass/Finding shape.
7. Import time and the REVIEW gate both call the shared Proof Admissibility
   registry/intake/evaluator and revalidate the current terminal, proposal,
   journal, prompt and material tuple.

Raw CLI output outside the trusted final-result adapter lane, usage-ledger rows, time-window correlations, pre-terminal
proposals, failed/cancelled/timed-out terminals and controller-authored verdicts
cannot upgrade to managed reviewer evidence. Raw same-UID CLI calls, forged
environment values, stale process groups, terminal/reaped runs and
ambiguous/multiple active candidates cannot borrow the descriptor authority.

The worker's reserved durable cancellation reason
`absolute_deadline_exceeded` always reconciles to a `timed_out` terminal with
that exact reason, even if the next observation occurs through the cancellation
branch. Human/operator cancellation remains `cancelled`; both paths retain the
same cleanup and replacement-safety proof.

The authority classifications remain disjoint. A native-host reviewer keeps the
signed ReviewRun plus direct ReviewPass/Finding path only when a registered
host-adapter broker signs the exact closeout invocation. Its Ed25519 attestation
binds Story, agent/lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch,
adapter/host identity and a one-shot nonce. Lattice stores the registered public
key and nonce-consumption record, but exposes no issuer command and stores no
broker private key. `dispatch`, `review_run_start`, inherited environment values
and raw provider CLIs cannot mint this authority. The host adapter must inject
the signed attestation over a dedicated descriptor for the exact CLI process;
without that integration, native direct evidence is advisory-only and formal
review must use the managed path.

Process ancestry is secondary evidence. An unobservable process table, as in a
brokered desktop sandbox, does not negate a valid broker signature. When a full
ancestry is observable, any mixed distinct provider families (Claude→Codex or
Codex→Claude) veto direct evidence even if the nearest ancestor matches. The
one-shot local nonce ledger prevents replay but is not represented as protection
against a same-UID/root attacker capable of replacing trusted configuration or
instrumenting the broker.

A cross-provider CLI reviewer requires a managed terminal receipt;
cross-provider CLI output without that receipt is advisory-only. An explicit
`degraded-single-host` fallback is local DONE assurance through host-verdict
evidence, not direct or managed REVIEW evidence, and cannot borrow either
reviewer authority path.

## Operator guidance

`lattice dispatch` prints two explicit execution modes. A native subagent uses
its host lifecycle. A cross-provider CLI reviewer must use `host_run
--managedReview`; raw `bash + codex/claude/agy` is advisory-only and cannot
satisfy the managed evidence path.

Poll the same run with `host_run_status --waitMs 30000`. Continue observing the
same run across silent intervals. Cancel only on an explicit operator decision.
Start a replacement only after an authoritative terminal and only when its
cleanup proves replacement safety.

## Retention and trust boundary

`lattice doctor` reports worker liveness, provider-progress observability,
deadline/cancel state, residuals, replacement safety and retention. Explicit
`doctor --repair` garbage-collects heavy terminal run directories only beyond
90 days and first revalidates sealed spec, result, event-journal, proposal and
evidence-binding digests, then preserves the minimal receipt plus evidence-binding
digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Any mismatch is reported as
corrupt and retained for manual review. The import-time evidence-binding seal is
checked before GC, and an expired cross-host run removes only its canonical
temporary detached snapshot. Active or corrupt runs and
runs that still contain one-shot inputs are retained fail-closed. Failed startup
removes one-shot secrets immediately.

The local filesystem boundary does not defend against a same-UID or root
attacker. Retained output may contain sensitive provider text and must be
treated accordingly.

## Compatibility and non-goals

- Existing finite provider timeouts, cross-host policy ceilings, bounded retry
  and fail-closed classifications remain in force.
- Ordinary non-review host runs remain compatible but now gain durable
  ownership and shared admission.
- No remote scheduler, daemon, queue or native-host subagent abstraction is
  introduced.
- Usage diagnostics remain non-authoritative and never become lifecycle proof.
